question: A machine-shop ledger ends with a value found by taking 4 J off a doubled figure, the doubling being for the shop's two identical benches. That doubled figure comes from a bench value that is what remains after a friction allowance of 16 J is subtracted from a run total, and the run total is 7 times the energy of a single launch. In one launch a carrier of 39 kg leaves the rail, and its launch speed in metres per second is the largest whole number that divides both 12 and 145 exactly, with nothing left over. The energy of a launch is the energy the carrier carries because of its motion as it leaves the rail. What value, in joules, ends the ledger?

A shunting locomotive pushes a wagon of 117 kg on a test rig, and the rate at which the wagon's acceleration builds, in metres per second cubed, follows 2t^2 + 3t. Between t = 0 seconds and t = 2 seconds the acceleration accumulates from zero, and the value reached at t = 2 seconds is the one used. From the force needed to drive the wagon at that acceleration the software subtracts a coupling tare of 27 N, then expresses the remainder in kilonewtons. That converted figure is multiplied by 8 for the 8 wagons in the rake, and a fixed contractual allowance of 20 kN is added at the end. The rig's siding is 40 m long, which plays no part in the calculation. What number, in kilonewtons, does the software report?

A calibration bench carries 8 identical reference masses, and the routine works through every distinct group of 4 that can be chosen from them. The number of such groups is, in metres per second squared, the acceleration the bench applies to a shuttle of 37 kg. The controller records the force needed to drive the shuttle and multiplies it by 3, since the routine is run on 3 axes. It expresses that total in kilonewtons and then subtracts a frame tare of 1 kN. The bench is 2 m wide, a dimension the controller records but never uses. What number, in kilonewtons, does the controller report?

A stores clerk counts 303 items in one bin and 356 in another, and works out the largest whole number that divides both counts exactly with nothing left over. A test slider of 11000 grams is released along a level bench at a speed, in metres per second, equal to that number. The bench software records the energy the slider carries because of its motion, then subtracts a friction allowance of 3 J, a bearing allowance of 16 J, and an air-drag allowance of 17 J in turn. Finally it adds a standing calibration offset of 9 J. What number, in joules, does the software report?

A test-house certificate carries a number found by adding a rigging allowance of 19 kN to a converted reading. That converted reading is the kilonewton form of the force needed to accelerate a sled of 72 kg along the house's rail. The acceleration used, in metres per second squared, is what remains when 26 is subtracted from the total of the squares of the whole numbers from 1 to 5. What number, in kilonewtons, appears on the certificate?

An engineer fits the curve 2x^3 - 5x^2 to a test trace, with x the elapsed time in seconds. The rate at which that fitted curve is changing at the instant x = 3 seconds gives a base figure, and adding a drive contribution of 15 to it gives the speed, in metres per second, of a carrier of 26 kg. The bench records the energy the carrier holds because of its motion at that speed, and a fixed instrument offset of 12 J is added to the record. The result is then expressed in kilojoules. The bench rail is 4 m long, a dimension that plays no part. What value, in kilojoules, does the bench report?

A hoist accelerates a load of 139000 grams, and the acceleration in metres per second squared is 9 times the sum of 3 and 2. The control system works out the force needed to drive the load and expresses it in kilonewtons. From that converted figure it subtracts a frame tare of 2 kN, then a contractual credit of 20 kN, and finally adds a rigging allowance of 1 kN. What number, in kilonewtons, does the control system report?

A machine shop fits the curve 3x^3 - 2x^2 to the recorded position, in metres, of a tool slide, with x the time in seconds. At the instant x = 3 seconds the rate at which the slope of that fitted curve is itself changing gives a base figure, and adding a drive contribution of 4 to it gives the acceleration, in metres per second squared, applied to a tool head of 21 kg. The controller records the force needed for that acceleration and multiplies it by 10, since 10 heads are driven together. It multiplies the result by 8 for the 8 slides on the machine, and then by 9 for the 9 machines in the shop. What figure, in newtons, does the controller report for the shop?

A teaching laboratory has 18 red weights and 101 blue weights, and the demonstrator works out the largest whole number that divides both counts exactly with nothing left over. A glider of 27000 grams is then released along the air track at a speed, in metres per second, equal to that number. The bench records the energy the glider carries because of its motion and multiplies it by 9, because 9 identical releases are made. The total is expressed in kilojoules, and a fixed instrument allowance of 22 kJ is added. The track is 2 m long, a dimension the bench never uses. What value, in kilojoules, does the bench report?

A press line drives a tool of 29 kg, and the rate at which its acceleration builds, in metres per second cubed, follows 3t^2 + 8t. Between t = 1 second and t = 3 seconds the acceleration accumulates from zero at the start of that interval, and the value reached at the end is the acceleration used. To the force needed to drive the tool at that acceleration the controller adds a die preload of 22 N. It multiplies the sum by 8 for the 8 tools on a press, by 11 for the 11 presses on the line, and by 10 for the 10 lines in the plant. The line's guard rail is 30 m long, a figure the controller never uses. What total, in newtons, does the controller report?

A logger fits the curve 5x^3 - 2x^2 to a trace, with x the time in seconds. The rate at which that fitted curve is changing at the instant x = 1 second gives, in metres per second, the speed of a probe of 11 kg. The system records the energy the probe carries because of its motion and expresses it in kilojoules. From that converted value a contractual credit of 22 kJ is subtracted, and the remainder is multiplied by 8 because 8 probes fly the same profile. The launch tower is 20 m tall, a height that never enters the calculation. What number, in kilojoules, does the system report?

A gantry report ends with a number that is 2 times an earlier total, because the hall has two identical gantries. That earlier total is 4 times a converted single-carriage reading, since each gantry carries 4 carriages. The converted reading is the kilonewton form of the force needed to accelerate one carriage of 58 kg along the beam, and the carriage's acceleration in metres per second squared is the rate at which its fitted position curve 1x^3 - 2x^2 is changing at the instant x = 2 seconds, with x the time in seconds and the position in metres. The beam spans 18 m, a length the report notes but does not use. What number, in kilonewtons, ends the report?

A launcher brings a puck of 10000 grams up to speed along a level rail, and the puck's acceleration in metres per second squared follows 2t^2 + 6t between t = 0 seconds and t = 1 second, starting from rest. The energy the puck carries because of its motion at the end of that interval is recorded and expressed in kilojoules. Because 9 pucks are fired in a run, 4 runs make a session, and 5 sessions make the study, the converted figure is multiplied by 9, then by 4, then by 5. The rail is 6 m long, a dimension that never enters the energy account. What total, in kilojoules, does the study report?

A quarry report closes with a number that is 9 times a site figure, because 9 sites run the same plant. Each site figure is 5 times a converted single-machine reading, since 5 machines work at a site. The converted reading is the kilonewton form of the force needed to accelerate a crusher jaw of 99 kg, and the acceleration in metres per second squared is what the rate curve 3t^2 + 4t accumulates between t = 0 seconds and t = 3 seconds, starting from zero and with t the time in seconds. What number, in kilonewtons, closes the report?

A vibration laboratory fits the curve 3x^3 - 3x^2 to a recorded trace, with x the time in seconds. At the instant x = 3 seconds the rate at which the slope of that fitted curve is itself changing gives, in metres per second, the speed of a test mass of 14 kg on the shaker. The bench records the energy the mass carries because of its motion, then subtracts a damping allowance of 25 J, a mounting allowance of 9 J, and finally adds a calibration offset of 3 J. The shaker head is 0.4 m across, a dimension the bench never uses. What number, in joules, does the bench report?

A teaching laboratory launches a trolley of 12 kg along a level rail. The trolley's launch speed in metres per second is the larger of the two values of x for which x^2 - 9x + 18 = 0. The bench records the energy the trolley carries because of its motion, multiplies it by 6 for the 6 launches in a demonstration, and multiplies that by 11 for the 11 demonstrations in the term. A fixed instrument allowance of 16 J is then added, and the total is multiplied by 12 because 12 laboratories run the same course. The rail is 3 m long, a length the bench never uses. What total, in joules, does the department record?

A rail test bench launches a carriage of 24000 grams. Its launch speed in metres per second is found by taking 5 times the sum of 2 and 17 and then subtracting a slip loss of 20 from the result. The bench records the energy the carriage carries because of its motion and expresses that record in kilojoules. From the converted figure a contractual credit of 2 kJ is subtracted, and a standing allowance of 10 kJ is added afterwards. What value, in kilojoules, does the bench report?

A conveyor report ends with a figure that is 5 times the force needed for one push, because 5 pushers act together. Each push accelerates a crate of 160000 grams along the belt. The acceleration in metres per second squared is worked out from the sum of the whole numbers from 1 to 12, to which a drive contribution of 4 is added and from which a friction loss of 24 is then subtracted. What figure, in newtons, ends the report?

A quarry ledger closes with a number that is 20 N more than a site total. The site total is 9 times a line figure, and the line figure is 3 times a station value, since 9 lines and 3 stations are involved. Each station value is what you get by adding a bearing preload of 27 N to the force needed to accelerate a hopper of 178 kg. The hopper's acceleration in metres per second squared is the largest whole number that divides both 96 and 20 exactly, with nothing left over. What number, in newtons, closes the ledger?

A drop-test laboratory keeps 9 identical reference masses and tests every distinct pair that can be chosen from them. The number of such pairs is, in metres per second, the release speed of a carrier of 53000 grams on the laboratory's rail. The bench records the energy the carrier carries because of its motion and expresses that record in kilojoules. It then subtracts a rig allowance of 19 kJ and, after that, a further handling allowance of 10 kJ. What value, in kilojoules, does the bench report?

A press-shop summary ends with a number found by taking a contractual credit of 12 kN off a converted total. That converted total is the kilonewton form of a figure that is 12 times the force needed for one stroke, since 12 strokes make a cycle. In one stroke a tool of 25000 grams is accelerated, and its acceleration in metres per second squared is what the rate curve 4t^2 + 4t accumulates between t = 0 seconds and t = 3 seconds, starting from zero, with t the time in seconds. What number, in kilonewtons, ends the summary?

A launcher brings a carriage of 23 kg up to speed along a level track, and the carriage's acceleration in metres per second squared follows 4t^2 + 8t. Between t = 1 second and t = 3 seconds the speed builds from rest at the start of that interval, and the speed reached at the end is the one recorded. The logger records the energy the carriage carries because of its motion at that speed and multiplies it by 3 for the 3 carriages in a run, by 2 for the 2 runs in a session, and by 10 for the 10 sessions in the programme. The programme total is then expressed in kilojoules. The track is 80 m long, a length the logger never uses. What total, in kilojoules, does the logger report?

A teaching bench launches a trolley of 51 kg along a level rail. The trolley's launch speed in metres per second is the smaller of the two values of x for which x^2 - 9x + 18 = 0. The bench records the energy the trolley carries because of its motion and multiplies it by 2, because 2 trolleys are launched together. A fixed instrument offset of 7 J is added, and the total is then expressed in kilojoules. The rail stands 0.8 m above the floor, a height the bench never uses. What value, in kilojoules, does the bench report?

A test summary ends with a number found by taking a calibration credit of 1 kJ off a converted reading. That converted reading is the kilojoule form of a value obtained by adding a fixed instrument offset of 21 J to the energy a projectile of 41000 grams carries because of its motion. The projectile's speed in metres per second is found by taking the larger of the two values of x for which x^2 - 12x + 32 = 0 and adding a drive contribution of 17 to it. What number, in kilojoules, ends the summary?

A demonstration rig on a lecture bench launches a puck of 2 kg across a smooth surface. The puck's launch speed in metres per second is the smaller of the two values of x for which x^2 - 7x + 10 = 0. The bench records the energy the puck carries because of its motion and adds a fixed instrument offset of 25 J to the record. That sum is multiplied by 10, because 10 launches make a demonstration, and the total is expressed in kilojoules. The demonstration is repeated in 6 lecture theatres, and the converted totals are added, giving the departmental figure. The bench is 1.4 m wide, a dimension that plays no part. What is the departmental figure, in kilojoules?
